newsitem.title: USA: KKK sues South Carolina sheriff for harassment.
newsitem.headline: KKK sues South Carolina sheriff for harassment.

text.p: The Christian Knights of the Ku Klux Klan, in the public spotlight since two members confessed to burning down predominantly black churches, have filed a lawsuit claiming a local sheriff harassed them.

In the federal lawsuit filed Tuesday, the local Klan group said Sheriff Hoyt Collins denied them their constitutional right to freedom of speech and assembly by intimidating members and singling them out for selective enforcement of laws. Members were searched without cause and deputies pointed guns at them and tore down their signs, it said.
Members suffered "grave emotional distress" and their reputations were injured, the lawsuit said. The harassment was so strong leaders considered returning the group's charter.
Collins denied the allegations. "I allowed them to assemble," he said Wednesday, while acknowledging that he monitored the group closely.
"This is not Dodge city and that's not allowed under the Constitution," said Gary White, a lawyer for the Klan. He said the group was censored because its message was unpopular.

A lawsuit brought by two local churches burned by Klan members is pending against the Christian Knights. Two members pleaded guilty this year to burning down Mount Zion AME Church in Greeleyville, visited by President Clinton in June, and Macedonia Baptist church in Bloomville.
